title: 3/8 charge-density wave instability in the kagome metal CsV$_3$Sb$_5$
authors: Luca Buiarelli, Hyeonseo H. Park, Ethan T. Ritz, Rafael M. Fernandes, Turan Birol
abstract: The kagome metal CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ exhibits charge density wave (CDW) and superconducting transitions, both of which are substantially affected by pressure. Recent x-ray diffraction experiments identify a new charge-ordered phase at a pressure coinciding with the dip of the superconducting dome. This CDW phase displays a distinctive wavevector $\mathbf{Q} = (3/8, 0, 1/2)$ and monoclinic symmetry, in contrast to the $2\times2\times 2$ and $2\times2\times 4$ orders reported at ambient pressure. In this letter, we show that density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) calculations on a fine reciprocal-space grid predict the leading lattice instability of CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ to be at this wavevector. Finite-displacement calculations reveal that while anharmonic effects stabilize the conventional $L_2^-$ CDW at ambient pressure, the competing $3/8$ instability becomes energetically favorable above $\sim$1 GPa, consistent with experimental observations. Interestingly, the nesting function displays a peak at the same wavevector. A Landau free energy analysis explains the emergence of the monoclinic distortion observed in x-ray diffraction, in addition to several bond-ordering patterns that may be relevant to the observed trends in the superconducting $T_c$.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the charge density wave (CDW) instability in the kagome metal CsV3Sb5, finding that the dominant instability switches from one type to another as pressure increases. By combining advanced DFT calculations with Landau theory, the authors map out the phase diagram, explaining the observed structural transitions and their connection to the superconducting state.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the leading lattice instability (Charge Density Wave, CDW) in the kagome metal CsV3Sb5 and understand how this instability changes with applied pressure relative to superconducting transitions.
main_result: The analysis predicts that the CDW instability switches from a conventional L-2 type at ambient pressure to a new R3 instability above approximately 1 GPa, consistent with experimental observations.
method: The authors employed Density Functional Perturbation Theory (DFPT) calculations, finite-displacement DFT, and a Landau free energy analysis to model the competing electronic and lattice instabilities.
model_or_system: The physical system is the kagome metal CsV3Sb5. The theoretical framework involves analyzing the competition between multiple order parameters (M, L, Sigma, R) using a complex free energy functional derived from symmetry considerations.
key_observables: CDW wavevectors (Q), phonon frequencies (imaginary parts), superconducting critical temperature (Tc), and lattice distortions (monoclinic symmetry).
important_parameters: Pressure (P), specifically the transition point near 1 GPa, and the relative strengths of anharmonic coupling terms in the free energy functional.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the R3 mode is the leading instability based on fine-grid DFPT calculations, and that the free energy can be accurately modeled by coupling the four primary order parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phonon instabilities across different Q-grids, show the pressure evolution of imaginary phonon frequencies for L-2 and R3 modes, and compare total energy/enthalpy curves to map the phase transition between the two CDW states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the initial instability using DFPT on fine grids, to comparing the stability of competing modes (L-2 vs R3) using finite-displacement calculations, and finally constructing a comprehensive Landau free energy functional to explain the coexistence and transition between multiple ordered phases.
why_interesting: While focused on CDW physics, the detailed analysis of competing order parameters, phase transitions driven by external fields (pressure), and the use of symmetry-constrained free energy functionals are highly relevant to understanding complex many-body ground states in correlated materials.

The displacement on the horizontal axis is the root-sum-of-squares displacement normalized by the square root of the supercell size relative to the primitive cell. The contrasting pressure sensitivity of the two modes is the key result: the L− 2 minimum rises rapidly with pressure (b) while the R3 minimum remains comparatively stable (c), switching the most stable phase near 1 GPa.

Apart from the different periodicities (2 unit cells along [100] for L− 2 , as opposed to 8 unit cells for R3), both modes are well described as nearest-neighbor bond order between the V ions. The pressure dependence of the unstable phonon branch near L is shown in Figs. 1(e–f). Both the R3 and L− 2 instabilities exhibit only a small change in frequency up to ∼0.8 GPa, above which both of their frequencies decrease in absolute magnitude sharply, and continue to decrease with pressure afterwards.
